faqs.title: FAQ
faqs.subtitle: Questions about parser scope and next steps

item-1.question: What does AwemeFlow do right now?
item-1.answer: It parses Douyin share text, short links, and aweme IDs into usable video URLs and structured metadata.

item-2.question: Is this already ready for Cloudflare?
item-2.answer: Yes. The current app structure has already been aligned with Cloudflare-friendly deployment and has been building successfully.

item-3.question: Does it already support API access?
item-3.answer: Not as a polished public product layer yet. The current focus is parser reliability and a strong single-input frontend.

item-4.question: Why hide blog, docs, and test pages?
item-4.answer: Because they dilute the product story. Keeping them out of the public surface makes the site feel like one focused parser product.

item-5.question: How do I report a broken example or ask for API access?
item-5.answer: Use the contact page or beta list and include the failed sample, expected workflow, or volume requirement.

testimonials.title: Use cases
testimonials.subtitle: Who this parser is currently good for

item-1.name: Content operator
item-1.quote: Paste the share text, get the usable video URL, and move on without extra cleaning steps.

item-2.name: Research analyst
item-2.quote: The parser is most useful when you need covers, author data, and source links fast for account analysis.

item-3.name: Workflow builder
item-3.quote: The current frontend is simple, but the output shape is already close to what an internal API flow would need.

item-4.name: PM or founder
item-4.quote: This version is good for validating whether parser demand and repeat usage are real before adding heavier commercial layers.

item-5.name: Content team lead
item-5.quote: Once batch parsing and quota layers are added, the product can naturally move from solo use to team use.

item-6.name: Deployment owner
item-6.quote: The app is already in a shape where shipping a clean first version on Cloudflare is much more realistic.

item-7.name: Operator
item-7.quote: The big win is that the parser now sits at the center of the product instead of being buried under template furniture.

item-8.name: Commercial buyer
item-8.quote: The current site makes it clear what will become paid later: volume, API access, and steadier team workflows.

item-9.name: Quality loop owner
item-9.quote: The real product moat here is not page count. It is parser success rate, fast issue feedback, and usable output.

item-10.name: Growth owner
item-10.quote: A tighter single-product story usually converts better than exposing every leftover template surface.

item-11.name: Infra-minded builder
item-11.quote: This is now much closer to a launchable parser MVP than to a generic SaaS boilerplate demo.

item-12.name: Roadmap watcher
item-12.quote: The next useful moves are batch parsing, API access, and better failure reporting, not more template pages.

stats.title: Signals
stats.subtitle: What matters for this product
stats.description: AwemeFlow should be judged by parser usefulness, repeat usage, and deployment speed rather than generic SaaS vanity metrics.

calltoaction.title: Start with a cleaner parser product
calltoaction.description: Use the current site to validate demand, collect failed samples, and prepare for API, batch, and team layers.
